entities.text: High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: CORAM : HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RATNAKER BHENGRA -------

For the Petitioner : Mr. Kumar Harsh, Advocate  For the State : Mr. Azeemuddin, APP  --------
05 /13.09.2024  I.A. No. 7469 of 2024  Heard the learned counsels for the parties.

The instant interlocutory application has been filed on behalf of the petitioner for stay against the order dated 26.09.2023 passed by the learned Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bermo at Tenughat; whereby and whereunder the learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Bokaro has issued distress warrant against the petitioner in connection with Original Maintenance Case ( M.P.) No. 95 of 2015.
The instant criminal revision has been filed for quashing and setting aside the order dated 29.08.2023 passed in Maintenance Alteration Case No. 13/2021 arising out of Original Maintenance Case (M.P.) No. 95 of 2015 by the learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Bokaro.
It is submitted that the O.P. No. 2 had filed complaint Case No. 392 of 2015 and under provisions of section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C. FIR was registered being Bokaro Thermal P.S. Case No. 135 of 2015 for the offence under sections 323, 498A, 497, 420, 406, 387/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
It is further submitted that the petitioner was convicted in this case by the learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Bermo at Tenughat for the offence under sections 323/387/494/497/498 of Md. Samsul vs The State Of Jharkhand on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125475908/
1 the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text:
Thereafter the petitioner preferred an appeal which was numbered as Cr.
Appeal No. 139 of 2019 and vide judgment and order dated 15.12.2021 the learned Additional Sessions Judge-1, Bermo at Tenughat allowed the appeal of the petitioner and set aside the conviction of the petitioner.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-1, Bermo at Tenughat
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the meantime, the petitioner was dismissed from his service vide order dated 18.07.2020.
thereafter he approached before the M/s. CCL for reinstatement of his service and thereafter he was reinstated in service on 10.05.2023.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that however, he was not given his back wages for the period he was dismissed and therefore he was unable to pay pay regular maintenance amount or substantial amount and therefore the counsel has prayed in the instant interlocutory application for stay against the order dated 26.09.2023 passed by the learned Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bermo at Tenughat whereby and whereunder the learned Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bermo at Tenughat has issued distress warrant against the petitioner in connection with Original Maintenance Case (M.P.) No. 95 of 2015.
The learned counsel for the petitioner has further submitted that the petitioner the ready and willing to resume making payments on installment wise.

Having heard the learned counsels for both the sides, having noted the submissions and gone through the records of the case that are available and the contents of the I.A. No. 7469 of 2024 and the submission of the petitioner, the distress warrant issued against the petitioner in connection with Original Maintenance Case ( M.P.) No. 95 of 2015 passed by the learned Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bermo at Tenughat vide order dated 26.09.2023 is stayed.
Accordingly, I.A. No. 7469 of 2024 stands allowed and disposed of.

Issue notice to the O.P. No 2 through registered post with A/D as well as by ordinary process for which requisites etc. must be filing within two weeks, thereafter list this case on 18.10.2024.
(Ratnaker Bhengra, J.) Sharda/
